cards.sense: Able to learn, understand and think well.
cards.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary — US English pronunciation
cards.simple_meaning: Able to learn, understand and think well.
cards.explanation: An intelligent person or animal can solve problems and learn new things. Intelligence grows when we stay curious and keep practising.
cards.example_sentence: Our science teacher told us that crows are intelligent birds that can use sticks as tools.
cards.real_world_usage: That was an intelligent idea to use the old bottles for our garden project!
cards.spelling_guidance: Remember the double l in the middle and the -ent ending: intel-li-gent.
cards.learning_objective: Use 'intelligent' to describe people, animals or ideas that show good thinking and learning.
cards.illustration_brief: A crow on a garden wall using a small stick to pull food out of a narrow container, while two children watch with wonder.

cards.sense: A piece of art made by carving or shaping stone, wood, clay or metal.
cards.ipa_source: CMU Pronouncing Dictionary — US English pronunciation
cards.simple_meaning: A piece of art made by carving or shaping stone, wood, clay or metal.
cards.explanation: A sculpture is art you can walk around and see from all sides, not a flat picture. The artist who makes it is called a sculptor.
cards.example_sentence: On our school trip to the museum, we saw an ancient stone sculpture of a dancer.
cards.real_world_usage: We made a clay sculpture of an elephant in our art class.
cards.spelling_guidance: The artwork ends in -ture (sculpture), but the artist ends in -or (sculptor).
cards.learning_objective: Recognise a sculpture as a three-dimensional artwork and distinguish 'sculpture' from 'sculptor'.
cards.illustration_brief: Children in a museum gallery looking at a carved stone sculpture of a graceful dancer on a pedestal, with a clay model of an elephant on a nearby table.
